title: Bridge a CT circuit at its test terminals, then open its links
instruction: Take the black two-pin bridge from its holder and push it fully into the two test sockets nearest you on terminals 2S1 and 2S2 (the pair with yellow markers), then let go. After that, take the screwdriver from its stand and, on each of those two terminals, put the blade down the slot and push the slide at its bottom away from you until it stops. The bridge must be in before either slide moves. Do not touch the terminals with red or blue markers.
context: Before a protection relay or meter is tested, the current-transformer circuit feeding it is shorted on the CT side of its test-disconnect terminals with a plug-in bridge, and only then are the terminals' disconnect links opened. Opening a link first, or bridging the relay-side sockets instead, open-circuits a working CT secondary, which can rise to kilovolts and arc; crews tell the circuits apart by their terminal markers. Each link's slide sits at the bottom of its narrow, deep slot, where it is hard to see, so one hand can watch the slot from above while the other works the screwdriver.
setup: Positions are from the arm bases (forward of the line joining the two bases, which are 61 cm apart; left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot; heights above the table top). Mounting plate: a light-grey 6 mm steel plate (17.9 cm front to back, 10.8 cm left to right) on a dark 6 mm spacer (12 x 8.8 cm), fixed to the table, its top 1.2 cm above the table, spanning 17.6 to 35.5 cm in front of the bases, centred on the midline. Terminal row: a 35 mm DIN rail (NS 35/7.5) runs left-right across the plate 28 cm in front of the bases; on it six grey Phoenix Contact URTK/S test-disconnect terminal blocks (0311087; each 8.2 mm wide, 61 mm long, 58.6 mm tall on the rail, their tops 7.06 cm above the table) lie face up with their long axis pointing away from the robot, spanning 24.95 to 31.05 cm in front of the bases. From the robot's left their centres are 2.27, 1.45, 0.41 cm left and 0.41, 1.45, 2.27 cm right of the midline: terminals 1S1 and 1S2 (circuit 1), a 2.2 mm dark-grey partition plate, 2S1 and 2S2 (circuit 2), a partition plate, 3S1 and 3S2 (circuit 3), with 2.2 mm end covers at both ends. Each terminal has a slot along its middle (7.2 mm wide, 40 mm long, 22 mm deep) holding two 4 mm test sockets (modelled as 4.8 mm square holes, 17 mm deep, their mouths 4 mm below the terminal's top) 14 mm on either side of the slot's centre (the CT-side socket 26.6 cm and the relay-side socket 29.4 cm in front of the bases), and at the slot's bottom the disconnect slide: a 9 x 5 mm nickel-plated slide with a 6 mm lug at each end, which closes the link in its home position and opens it when pushed 2.5 mm or more away from the robot (5 mm to its stop). Each terminal carries a printed marker strip (7.6 x 4.4 mm, ZB 8 style) on the top of both ends, coloured by circuit: circuit 1 red, circuit 2 yellow, circuit 3 blue. In front of each circuit a card of the same colour (17.4 mm wide, 28 mm front to back, printed CT1, CT2 or CT3) lies on the plate 19.1 to 21.9 cm in front of the bases; a white label printed 'FROM CTs (CT side)' lies on the plate's front edge and one printed 'TO RELAY 87B' beyond the row. Black wires (visual only) leave both ends of each terminal. Bridge: a Phoenix Contact KSS 8 two-pole plug-in short-circuit connector (0311540; black polyamide grip 15 mm wide, 9 mm thick, 19 mm tall; two 4 mm pins 20 mm long, 8.2 mm apart; 8 g), standing pins down in a grey holder (a 16 x 22 mm column with two dummy sockets, its top 7.06 cm above the table) centred 20 cm in front of the bases and 13 cm left of the midline, the pins left-right. Screwdriver: an insulated VDE slotted screwdriver (0.6 x 3.5 mm class; red 22 mm square handle 7 cm long with a yellow band, 5 cm shaft, 3.5 mm blade; 45 g), standing blade down in a dark-grey stand (3 x 3 cm, 9 cm tall, 6 mm hole) centred 20 cm in front of the bases and 14 cm right of the midline, the blade's 3.5 mm width left-right, the handle resting on the stand's top. All six slides start closed. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: A pin counts as in a socket when its tip is inside the socket and at least 10 mm below the terminal's top (6 mm into the socket); the bridge is seated when both pins are in sockets and its grip is within 1.5 mm of resting on the terminals' tops. A link counts as open when its slide has moved 2.5 mm or more from home. Score 0 if, at any time before the after-release check: a 2S1 or 2S2 link is open while the bridge's two pins are not in the CT-side sockets of 2S1 and 2S2 (the CT would be open-circuited); a link of circuit 1 or 3 is open; both pins are in any other pair of sockets (the relay-side sockets of circuit 2 included); or a fingertip (6 mm from the finger's end), a pin tip of the bridge or the screwdriver's blade tip comes lower than 1 cm above the top of a red- or blue-marked terminal while over it. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if the bridge has moved 1 cm or more from its place in the holder; 0.5 if it is seated in the CT-side sockets of 2S1 and 2S2; 0.75 if, with it seated there, both 2S1 and 2S2 links are open; 1.0 if the after-release check also passes. After-release check, once both grippers have been at least 5 cm from the bridge for 2 s: pull the bridge's grip with a spring scale at 5 N along the rail toward the robot's left for 1.5 s, then at 5 N toward the robot for 1.5 s. It passes if both pins stay in the CT-side sockets of 2S1 and 2S2 throughout and both links are still open at the end; if not, the score is 0.75. Dropping the bridge is not penalised by itself. Slide travel is measured with calipers from the slide's lug to the slot's end.
reset_notes: Push both 2S slides back toward the robot to their home position, then pull the bridge out and stand it back in its holder, pins left-right (on a working panel the links are always closed before the bridge comes out). Stand the screwdriver blade down in its stand, blade left-right. Check that all six slides are home. About 1 minute. Real trials use a spare, unwired terminal row on the bench, never a working CT circuit; if a test lamp is wanted, use a battery continuity tester across the sockets.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Terminal pitch/size and bridge pins from Phoenix datasheets; slot, socket depth and slide travel inferred from photos (no CAD). Box colliders; rigid pins hold the bridge by geometry. Row lies face up; slide clamp screw not modelled (spring detent instead); screwdriver shortened. No circuit: short/open are rules on pin and slide positions. Coloured markers; tug in sim after recording. Details in README.
